concepts.explanation: The heart suddenly stops beating. Different from a heart attack, which is a blocked artery.
A blocked artery starving part of the heart of blood. Commonly called a heart attack.
A life-threatening overreaction to infection that can shut down organs.
Inserting a tube into the airway so a machine can breathe for the patient.
Medical shorthand for immediately, from the Latin statim.
Hospital alert that a patient's heart or breathing has stopped and resuscitation is needed now.
A patient's instruction not to attempt CPR or revival if their heart or breathing stops.
Sorting patients by urgency so the most critical are treated first.
A severe, fast allergic reaction that can close the airway. Treated with adrenaline.
Cancer spreading from where it started to other parts of the body. Stage four means it has done so.
Drugs that kill fast-dividing cells to treat cancer, with side effects on healthy cells too.
Removing a small tissue sample to examine it for disease, usually cancer.
A bulge in a weakened blood vessel wall. If it bursts, bleeding can be fatal within minutes.
Blood supply to part of the brain cut off by a clot or bleed, killing brain cells.
A brain injury from a blow to the head causing confusion, headache or memory loss.
A disease spreading across countries or continents. An epidemic is regional; a pandemic is global.
A preparation training the immune system to recognise a pathogen without causing the disease.
Bacteria evolving to survive antibiotics, making common infections harder to treat.
Powerful painkillers including morphine and fentanyl. Highly addictive; overdose stops breathing.
US law protecting the privacy of medical records.
Prolonged unconsciousness. Doctors sometimes induce it deliberately to let the brain heal.
Losing contact with reality, such as hallucinations or fixed false beliefs.
A study where some patients get a dummy treatment and neither they nor the doctors know who, to test a drug fairly.
